children: Chicago Mercantile Exchange feeder cattle futures rose on Tuesday as US beef prices increased and slaughtering recovered following disruptions linked to an immigration crackdown, analysts said.

Meatpackers processed an estimated 108,000 cattle, after daily slaughtering had dropped below 100,000 over the past week, according to USDA data. The total was in line with levels before the immigration crackdown discouraged meatpacking employees from going to work at major slaughterhouses in southwest Kansas last week.

Processing rates can influence cattle prices by affecting meatpackers' demand. Disruptions can back up cattle in feedlots and threaten cash prices because packers may not need to bid aggressively to make purchases.
"The biggest factor in the cattle market right now is packing," AgMarket.net CFO Tyler Schau said in a note.
"If that remains near normal levels over the coming days, we may be able to move past this latest disruption."

Rising boxed beef prices supported futures, traders said. Choice cuts of boxed beef increased by $2.18 to $382.66 per hundredweight, while select cuts climbed by $6.25 to $364.48 per cwt, according to USDA.
The agency separately quoted the wholesale pork carcass cutout at $87.77 per cwt, down 3 cents from Monday. Pork bellies climbed $6.73 to $99.32 per cwt.
CME December lean hog (LHZ26) futures closed up 1.30 cents at 69.700 cents per pound. Deferred futures months set contract lows.
